sources.title: Community Right to Bid: non-statutory advice note for local authorities
sources.verified_claim: The official advice summarises Localism Act and 2012 Regulations; listing creates a disposal moratorium process but not a right of first refusal.

sources.title: Assets of community value
sources.verified_claim: Enfield accepts qualifying nominations and explains a six-month community-bid window if a listed owner intends to sell; listing does not identify parcel_30762 without register matching.

sources.title: Assets of Community Value documents
sources.verified_claim: Havering publishes successful and unsuccessful nomination registers and guidance; register entries must be matched to exact land.

sources.title: Guidance for nominating land or property in Havering to be an asset of community value
sources.verified_claim: Havering requires site boundaries, ownership/occupier details and evidence of community value; a nomination is not an accepted listing.

sources.title: Assets of community value
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth explains the Community Right to Bid and six-month bid-preparation period; it does not give communities a right to buy.

sources.title: What types of property can be listed?
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth sets eligibility tests and exclusions, including residential property; exact current/recent use is required for listing.

sources.title: Assets of community value downloads
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth publishes nomination forms and historical successful/unsuccessful lists; historic lists do not prove current status without checking the exact entry.

sources.title: Assets of Community Value
sources.verified_claim: Somerset notes 2026 legislation introduces future changes but the relevant ACV provisions are not yet in force until regulations/guidance commence; current law remains the existing scheme.
